subject: Post-demo: compact shortlist + perf/ops checks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@quantbyte.com>, Julia Park <julia.park@quantbyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: compact shortlist + perf/ops checks

Hi Alex / Julia —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear context about your customer scenarios (transactional chat + short document summarization). Quick recap and our recommended compact shortlist so you can move to a focused one-week evaluation:

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs at a glance)
- Redwood-7B-q4 (recommended pilot): lowest cost per token, excellent 95ms median latency on our infra, good factuality after prompt tuning for short responses. Best fit if you need predictable cost and sub-150ms p50.
- OpenLlama-13B-quant (balanced): higher baseline quality on multi-turn coherence, medium latency (p95 ~220ms) with quantization; good choice if you expect longer context and a higher tolerance for cost.
- LLaMA2-70B-8bit (quality-first): top quality for complex summarization but significantly higher inference cost and p95 latency (500ms+ without aggressive batching). Use as fallback for heavy docs or where quality trumps latency.

Notes / risks
- Hallucination sensitivity: on the demo prompts we saw a ~3% hallucination rate for Redwood-7B-q4 vs ~1.2% for LLaMA2-70B; prompt engineering + instruction-tuning reduces that gap for short form responses.
- Tail latency: if you hit concurrent spikes above ~8 req/s on a single instance, p95 for the 13B quant model climbs; we can mitigate with sharding and autoscale but cost increases.

What we shared (attached & links)
- benchmark_summary.csv — pooled latency and cost numbers from today
- prompt_pack-v1.jsonl — the post-demo prompt set we used for scoring and regression checks
- internal bench results: https://redwood.internal/bench/2027-08-21/qb-demo (read-only)

Next steps (suggested, short):
1) Confirm throughput target and p95 SLO — you mentioned ~10 req/s and 200ms p95 during the call. Please confirm.
2) We suggest a 1-week A/B eval: Redwood-7B-q4 (pilot) vs OpenLlama-13B-quant (higher quality) with the shared prompt pack. We’ll run the same prompt set and share regression metrics (accuracy, hallucination, latency, cost).
3) If you want, we can add LLaMA2-70B behind a fallback route for long-doc queries only.

If confirmed, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff early next week with Ben and Monica to set up the eval runs and instrumentation (regression checks, logging, alerting thresholds).

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmark_summary.csv (csv), prompt_pack-v1.jsonl (jsonl)
From: Alex Chen <alex@quantbyte.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@quantbyte.com>, salesops@quantbyte.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: compact shortlist + perf/ops checks

Thanks, Soojin — great recap and clear asks. Quick answers:
- Throughput target: our immediate pilot target is 10 concurrent requests/sec (sustained), spike tolerance up to 25 req/s for short bursts.
- Latency SLO: our product team wants p95 <= 200ms for the quick reply flow; for document summarization we can accept p95 <= 800ms.
- Hallucination: we have a low tolerance for factual drift on account IDs/transactions. Can you add an example of the hallucination instances you saw in the CSV? We’ll share an internal compliance checklist (uploading to your shared link) — earlier you mentioned guardrails and structured output support.

If Redwood-7B-q4 can meet the 200ms p95 at 10 req/s with low hallucination after prompt-pack tuning, that’s the most appealing path. Otherwise we’ll evaluate 13B quant with caching and a stricter fallback to 70B for long docs.

— Alex
Alex Chen 
Head of Product 
QuantByte
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: compact shortlist + perf/ops checks

FYI — forwarding Alex’s responses and confirming their targets (10 req/s sustained, 200ms p95 for quick replies). Action items for ops/bench:

> On Sun, 22 Aug 2027, Alex Chen wrote:
> > Throughput target: our immediate pilot target is 10 concurrent requests/sec (sustained)
> > Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for quick reply flow.

Proposed internal plan (short):
- Run synthetic bench with the exact prompt_pack-v1.jsonl (attached) at 10 req/s sustained and 25 req/s burst. Capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost for each model candidate.
- Priority for the first bench: Redwood-7B-q4 and OpenLlama-13B-quant. If 7B cannot meet 200ms p95 at 10 req/s on our standard node config, prepare a sharding/autoscale scenario and cost delta.
- Set up regression checks to flag hallucination rate >1.5% for pilot (we observed ~3% on 7B today; need to confirm if prompt tuning cuts it under 1.5%).
- Canary routing: start with 70% traffic to Redwood-7B-q4, 30% to 13B quant for 24 hours; fallback to LLaMA2-70B for any flagged queries (long-docs / low-confidence responses).

Deliverables and owner
- Bench artifacts + CSV: Ben (bench run + costs) — target EOD Wed 8/25.
- Prompt tuning pass & updated prompt pack: Monica — target Tue 8/24.
- Canaries and routing config: Soojin/Infra — target Thu 8/26.

I attached the prompt pack we used and the summary CSV. Also attached: quantbyte_sre_requirements.pdf from their message (moved to folder).

— Soojin

Attachments included: prompt_pack-v1.jsonl, benchmark_summary.csv, quantbyte_sre_requirements.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: compact shortlist + perf/ops checks

Got it — will run the synthetic bench today. Plan:
- Run Redwood-7B-q4 and OpenLlama-13B-quant at 10 req/s sustained and 25 req/s burst across our standard instance types; capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/second, and cost delta by model.
- Link to live bench run (read-only) will be posted to: https://redwood.internal/bench/2027-08-23/qb-live-run once started.
- If Redwood-7B-q4 misses 200ms p95 at 10 req/s, I’ll include a short appendix showing the autoscale cost to bring p95 under 200ms (sharding + +1 replica).

I’ll upload the bench CSV to the shared folder and tag the HubSpot deal (QB-2027-117). Monica — when you have the tuned prompt pack, attach it to the run so we can compare pre/post tuning hallucination rates.

— Ben
